To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prevalence of problematic Internet use is 6.2% in a general population of Norwegian adults and that it is strongly dependent on gender, age, and education.
1.0 percent of Norwegians are addicted to the Internet and 5.2 percent are at-risk users.
6.2% of the Norwegian population (1% Internet addicted, 5.2 % at risk) is affected by problematic Internet use, and the prevalence of Internet use disorders is highest among young males.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the prevalence of "problematic Internet usage" in the adult population, and with the identification of possible factors associated with this.
the prevalence and correlates of Internet addiction among Norwegian adults, and the relationship between Internet addiction and other psychological impairment.
the identification of the characteristics of the Internet users that are more likely to develop problematic Internet use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevalence of problematic Internet use in Norway is 1.0-6.2%, and is dependent on age and gender, with highest prevalence in the youngest age group and among young males.
Internet addiction and at risk of addiction are relatively rare in the general population.
the prevalence of Internet use is high in Norway and problematic Internet use is not uncommon, but not widespread.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Internet use has become an integral part of everyday life and that the Internet is an important source of entertainment, social contact, and information.
we have shown that Internet addiction is a real phenomenon that should not be neglected in clinical practice.
Internet addiction is a relatively rare disorder among the adult Norwegian population, but that a large proportion of Internet users are at risk of developing an addiction to the Internet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Internet addiction is an important public health problem.
the Internet is not a safe haven for people with psychological problems.
we have identified a group of young people who are at high risk for problematic Internet use.
